shouldFix.title: CA-1 IN_PROCESS is placed on the consentable roster as merely fail-closed-until-FC-C1, when both recorded host generations classify it UNEXERCISABLE in the architecture preview; it is the only roster member with no unexercisability clause, no fixture class, and no place on the fail-closed deny roster
evidence: The artifact defines its consentable host-side roster as exactly five members: 'CA-1 SPAWN decision (host head), CA-1 IN_PROCESS attempt, CA-2 process-creation decision, CA-3, and CA-4-HOST'. It then characterises all five identically: 'These require the host-effect contract (necessary, not sufficient) and remain fail-closed until FC-C1.' That characterisation says the thing standing between CA-1 IN_PROCESS and exercisability is FC-C1 plus sufficiency.

Both recorded host generations say otherwise, and they agree verbatim. host-effect v8 and v25 at /coveredActs/CA-1-host-head read: 'Doctor v4 CA-1 host-actor surface: SPAWN (child process) and IN_PROCESS. Only SPAWN can become exercisable under this contract's other gates. IN_PROCESS is classified and denied for the architecture preview.' The IN_PROCESS subtype's previewStanding reads: 'UNEXERCISABLE in the architecture preview. Classified so it cannot be relabeled as SPAWN. No in-process commit boundary is used because the subtype cannot pass.'

So IN_PROCESS is not a member of the class that becomes exercisable once FC-C1 is recorded and the contract is sufficient. It is co-classified with CA-2 and CA-3 KEYCHAIN. Both recorded generations state the grouping in one sentence: 'CA-1 SPAWN: DR-G21 + admitted manifest; CA-1 IN_PROCESS: unexercisable in the architecture preview; CA-2: unexercisable in the architecture preview, even with a DR-119 exception; CA-3 KEYCHAIN: DR-108, currently deferred so unexercisable'.

The artifact carries that unexercisability for two of the three and drops it for the third. CA-2 has an extracted clause saying it 'remains wholly unexercisable' plus three fixture classes (FC-JOIN-CA2-UNEXERCISABLE, FC-JOIN-CA2-D000-GATE, FC-JOIN-CA2-TAIL). CA-3 KEYCHAIN has an extracted clause ('still deferred, unexercisable'), ID-DEP-J5, and FC-JOIN-CA3-KEYCHAIN-UNEXERCISABLE. CA-1 IN_PROCESS has no clause, no identity dependency, and no fixture class.

I walked every occurrence of the token IN_PROCESS in the subject. There are exactly three: /extractedDecidedClauses/hostSideAttemptsOutsideDr105, /joinFixtureClasses/classes/0, and /honestyRepairsFromV1/0. All three are roster-membership recitals. The word 'unexercisable' appears eight times in the subject and never once within reach of IN_PROCESS.

The fail-closed deny roster is short by the same member. FC-JOIN-FAIL-CLOSED-UNRECORDED reads 'absence of joint-owner FC-C1 recording denies the consentable host-side roster (CA-1 host head, CA-2, CA-3, host CA-4)'. It names the roster by the artifact's own term and then lists four of its five members. The parenthetical mirrors D-032's four-item phrase rather than the artifact's own five-member definition.

The mechanism of the drop is an equivocation on 'host head' inside the subject. Two clauses bind the term to SPAWN specifically: componentTails says 'a host CA-1 SPAWN decision (the host head)' and the roster clause says 'CA-1 SPAWN decision (host head)'. Two other places use it in the inherited D-032 and v25 sense, where CA-1-host-head is the class covering both subtypes: hostEffectNecessaryNotSufficient and FC-JOIN-FAIL-CLOSED-UNRECORDED. Under the subject's own binding the deny roster omits IN_PROCESS; under the inherited binding the five-member roster double-counts. The subject does not say which binding governs.

This is not reachable by the v3 findings. CLAUDE-DAJ3-S1 was about the roll-up list, DAJ3-CX-01 about the admitted child's tail, DAJ3-CX-02 about CA-2's gates. None touched CA-1's second subtype, and the roster clause and FC-JOIN-FAIL-CLOSED-UNRECORDED are unchanged from v2 through v4, so this has stood unexamined for three generations.

The candidate applies nothing, binds NOTHING, the fixture classes are NAMED-NOT-AUTHORED, no corpus is executed, and FC-C1 is absent so no CA-1 attempt is exercisable today. That bounds the defect to SHOULD-FIX rather than a blocker, on the same reasoning Codex used to bound DAJ3-CX-01 and DAJ3-CX-02.
shouldFix.impact: A fixture corpus built from these twelve classes would assert fail-closed denial for four acts, unexercisability for CA-2 and CA-3 keychain, and nothing whatever about CA-1 IN_PROCESS. It would pass while running admitted component code in the doctor/host address space is treated as ordinarily consentable. The recorded generations classified the subtype precisely to prevent that: 'Classified so it cannot be relabeled as SPAWN.' This candidate's roster is the relabeling risk in miniature, because it presents the SPAWN decision and the IN_PROCESS attempt as co-equal members of one roster gated by one condition, when one becomes exercisable under the contract and the other cannot pass at all. The exposure lands the moment FC-C1 is recorded: at that point every stated gate for CA-1 IN_PROCESS in this artifact is satisfied, and the artifact contains no statement that would still deny it.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: State in an extracted clause that CA-1 IN_PROCESS is unexercisable in the architecture preview and cannot be relabeled as SPAWN, in the same form as the existing CA-2 and CA-3 keychain clauses, attributed to the recorded host-effect generations rather than to D-032. Add a fixture class, FC-JOIN-CA1-INPROCESS-UNEXERCISABLE or equivalent, asserting that CA-1 IN_PROCESS remains denied even when FC-C1 is recorded and the host-effect contract is otherwise sufficient. Either add CA-1 IN_PROCESS to the FC-JOIN-FAIL-CLOSED-UNRECORDED deny roster or state that its parenthetical uses 'CA-1 host head' in the class sense covering both subtypes, and fix the 'host head' equivocation so one binding governs throughout. Do not mint any grant, do not admit the subtype, and do not record FC-C1.

advisories.title: The new CA-2 D-000 gate sits under an extraction standing that attributes it to adopted D-032, which does not contain it
advisories.observation: The container's standing reads 'EXTRACTED from adopted D-032. Not re-decided here.' The two propositions v4 adds to the ca2 clause are not in the carried D-032 bytes: I byte-searched the thirty-four carried lines, normalised for the line wrapping and bold markers, and neither 'D-000' nor 'product/authorization' nor 'product owner' occurs. D-032 says only 'CA-2 also needs DR-119 (and DR-117/128 if third-party)'; it never says DR-119 is insufficient and never names a later decision. I also searched all of COORD: DR-119 co-occurs with CA-2 at exactly one line, 1640, which is D-032's own. No adopted decision anywhere establishes the gate. Its actual source is host-effect v8 and v25, which say 'a later D-000 product/authorization decision owned by the DR-119 product owner jointly with Security+platform is required before any CA-2 is exercisable' — and which this same artifact classifies as unapplied candidates that are not the FC-C1 recording. I do not grade this SHOULD-FIX for three reasons: the container has carried non-D-032 vocabulary since v2 with both reviewers' assent and a strict verbatim reading would condemn the typing repairs everyone asked for; the artifact states in three places that the D-000 decision does not exist and is not minted; and the direction is restrictive, so nothing can be admitted by it. Attributing the gate to the recorded host generations in the clause itself would remove the ambiguity at no cost.

advisories.title: FC-JOIN-COMPONENT-TAIL names 'representative non-egress child routes' without naming any, while every sibling class enumerates its members
advisories.observation: The DAJ3-CX-01 repair restores the broad rule correctly and the impact Codex named is defeated by that rule alone, so this is not a finding against the repair. But the class says 'representative non-egress child routes also stay in DR-105' and names none, where FC-JOIN-HOST-OUTSIDE-DR105 names its five acts exactly and FC-JOIN-HOST-DEFAULT-AND-OPMETA names its two families. The six non-egress routes are available and stable in both permission generations, which I re-verified rather than took: PT-FS-READ-PROJECT, PT-FS-READ-COMPONENT, PT-FS-WRITE-HOST-STATE, PT-PROC-EXEC-DECLARED, PT-ENV-READ, PT-HOST-EFFECT-BROKERED. Naming two or three would match the roster's own style without authoring fixtures.

verdictBasis: The dispatch permits ACCEPT only at zero blockers and zero SHOULD-FIX. This review returns zero blockers and one SHOULD-FIX, so the verdict is REJECT. All three v3 findings are genuinely repaired and I verified each by execution rather than by reading the repair notes: the roll-up list carries the sixth item, the component tail carries the broad rule with egress typed and the superseded phrase marked against its exact string, and the CA-2 route carries the D-000 gate whose existence I confirmed in both recorded host generations before crediting it. Custody, the closed roster, the carried D-032 block, the register row and all seventeen recorded inputs reproduce with zero mismatches. The finding came from a test this lineage has not run: a coverage matrix over the artifact's own five-member host-side roster, taking each member independently to the recorded host generations. Four reconcile. The fifth, CA-1 IN_PROCESS, is presented as an ordinary consentable attempt that is fail-closed until FC-C1, while host-effect v8 and v25 agree verbatim that it is UNEXERCISABLE in the architecture preview and was classified precisely 'so it cannot be relabeled as SPAWN'. The subject carries that unexercisability for its two co-classified siblings, CA-2 and CA-3 keychain, each with a clause and a fixture class, and carries nothing for this one; it also lists four of its own five roster members on the fail-closed deny roster, the mechanism being an unresolved equivocation on 'host head'. It is bounded to SHOULD-FIX for the reason Codex bounded the previous four findings: the candidate binds nothing, applies nothing, authors no fixtures, and FC-C1 is absent, so nothing is admitted today. It is nonetheless the one place where satisfying every gate this artifact states would leave a subtype exercisable that both recorded host generations deny.
